svg.title: Figure 3-SG-03-1. SG-03: from the fault tree to the FMEA
svg.desc: Figure 3-SG-03-1. SG-03: 29 events (backed 25, by design 1, external 3, unbacked 0); 43 FMEA modes reach SG-03 (in the tree 32, justified 11, tree gaps 0). Single points: BE-3.01: SWF-003, 3 causes, D 3–9, partly detected; BE-3.04: DFM-019, 2 causes, D 10, not detected; BE-3.11: SWF-017, SWF-006, 2 causes, D 3, every cause D ≤ 4: tree and FMEA disagree. BE-3.01 (Envelope accel upper bound (+2.0 m/s², toyota.h:208) above the controllable value; RAISED_ACCEL_LIMIT not validated for Corolla (toyota/interface.py:117-118; GAP-04; CCF → DFI-08)) → SWF-003: Acceleration request outside the intended envelope is passed; worst cause SWF-003.C1 (Panda upper bound +2.0 m/s² equals the SoC limit (RAISED_ACCEL_LIMIT is set for every TSS2 car, values.py:39-43) and is not derived from a validated Corolla envelope; no margin between controller and envelope; O 6, D 9, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause BE-3.04 (Frame corrupted after TX hook (as BE-1.10)) → DFM-019: Approved CAN frame altered between the TX check and the bus; worst cause DFM-019.C1 (Soft error or permanent fault in the copy into FDCAN message RAM, the message RAM or the FDCAN core. The packet XOR is checked at the FDCAN load (fdcan.h:100) and covers only the software queue; the CAN CRC is computed after the fault; O 3, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-3.02 (Planner/controller fault, wrong lead, e2e accel) → SFM-008, PFM-011: Unintended acceleration; worst cause SFM-008.C2 (Longitudinal controller output too high; O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: test_longcontrol.py covers state transitions, not limits BE-1.05 (Wrong CarParams / fingerprint (CCF → DFI-09)) → SFM-032, PFM-013, SWF-058: Wrong vehicle configuration active (fingerprint or car port); worst cause SWF-058.C2 (The FINGERPRINT environment variable overrides identification, and cached CarParams FW are reused when the VIN is known, so a replaced ECU is not re-queried (car_helpers.py:93-98, 140-142); O 2, D 10, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause BE-4.16 (Envelope software defect in the longitudinal checks (longitudinal_accel_checks, longitudinal.h:8-12)) → SWF-003, SWF-016: Acceleration request outside the intended envelope is passed; worst cause SWF-003.C1 (Panda upper bound +2.0 m/s² equals the SoC limit (RAISED_ACCEL_LIMIT is set for every TSS2 car, values.py:39-43) and is not derived from a validated Corolla envelope; no margin between controller and envelope; O 6, D 9, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause BE-1.07 (MCU execution fault (RAM/register/CPU) corrupts limit or check, not detected (no MPU, no ECC handling, faults report-only; GAP-08)) → DFM-001, DFM-002, DFM-003, DFM-005, DFM-007, DFM-018: Safety check computes a wrong result (permanent CPU or data-path fault); worst cause DFM-007.C1 (Vehicle supply dip (cranking, alternator fault) with BOR level not set and PVD not enabled; O 5, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-1.08 (Safety mode/param changed by SoC (0xdc, GAP-09) [FFI → FFI-CM-06; CCF → DFI-13: same SoC fault can cause G-SoC and BE-1.08]) → SWF-013, SWF-022: Wrong or permissive safety mode accepted from the host; worst cause SWF-022.C1 (setSafetyMode writes safety_configs[0] model and param and alternative_experience exactly as found in CarParams (panda_safety.cc:56-70). There is no allow-list for the reference configuration. A fingerprinting or CarParams error, such as a wrong EPS factor or flags, reaches the panda. At BL-004 the panda accepted any mode; at BL-005 the reference lock refuses anything but TOYOTA/73 (SWF-013), so the remaining effect is the safe direction (no engagement); O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause; test_pandad.py (hardware) checks only that pandad starts BE-1.09 (Envelope firmware replaced via boot pins / softloader (GAP-38, GAP-24) [FFI → FFI-CM-12; CCF → DFI-13]) → SWF-028, PFM-001, DFM-016, PFM-002, SWF-084: pandad runs against panda firmware that is not the assured reference build; worst cause SWF-028.C1 (pandad.py and up_to_date() compare the panda signature with the panda_h7.bin.signed built from the checkout (pandad.py:16-18, 29-49; panda.cc:116-127). At BL-004 that build was not LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE. At BL-005 it is by default, and pandad checks the reference-build flag (TSR-619). Remaining: the flag says "a reference build", not "the assured release image" (any LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE build of any commit sets it), and a build opted out on both sides passes; O 5, D 10, AP H); detection: No host test of the pandad check. The panda side (flag set only in the reference build) is unit-tested in panda CI; the release build check is in CI (SWF-013.C2). Neither is designed to detect a non-assured reference image UE-3.05 (PCM executes request without its own bound (AOU-05R fails)): No FMEA row needed: external; AOU-05R BE-4.17 (Host sends a step: the CarController jerk limit is applied before pitch compensation and the PID (carcontroller.py:197-238)) → SWF-046, SWF-066: ACC acceleration command differs from controlsd's request (higher, lower or faster changing) within the panda range; worst cause SWF-046.C2 (controlsd passes aTarget through unchanged up to the panda limits (LongControl is feed-forward for Toyota, ki=kp=0, interfaces.py:212-214; limits = ACCEL_MIN/MAX, toyota/interface.py:21-22), so the host adds no margin or jerk bound of its own; O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: test_longcontrol.py covers state transitions, not limits BE-3.03 (No jerk limit in envelope: step to +2.0 m/s² allowed (GAP-04, FSR-03.03 not implemented)) → SWF-004: Step change of deceleration request to the minimum is passed; worst cause SWF-004.C1 (longitudinal_accel_checks checks the range only; no rate or jerk limit on acceleration requests; O 8, D 9, AP H); detection: No test targets this cause BE-3.06 (SoC requests positive accel in a closing situation) → SFM-008, PFM-011: Unintended acceleration; worst cause SFM-008.C2 (Longitudinal controller output too high; O 7, D 10, AP H); detection: test_longcontrol.py covers state transitions, not limits BE-3.07 (Envelope passes any in-bound value while authority is granted (by design)): No FMEA row needed: by design; The envelope passes any in-bound request while authority is granted; the hazard is the request (G3.2). UE-3.08 (Driver does not brake in time (controllability; AOU-06R)): No FMEA row needed: external; AOU-06R (WP-C-03 HE-03.1…03.3 controllability, C2 credits AOU-03/AOU-05) BE-1.12 (Corrupted/replayed 0x1D2 creates false cruise rising edge with valid 8-bit checksum (no counter, GAP-01)) → SWF-007: Controls allowed without a driver engagement; worst cause SWF-007.C1 (Defect in pcm_cruise_check or PCM_CRUISE decoding (toyota.h rx hook, 0x1D2 bit 5); O 5, D 3, AP H); detection: opendbc safety suite with 100% line coverage and mutation tests, run by fork CI on every change (.github/workflows/safety.yaml, CR-CI-05). At BL-002 the Toyota tests pass locally (287, 34 skipped); mutation was last run locally at BL-001 (2705/2705 killed). Tests are derived from the implementation, not from requirements BE-1.13 (Panda RX path delivers stale/stuck cruise frame to both envelope and SoC (single RX path; CCF → DFI-10)) → SWF-006: Stale brake, cruise or EPS data used beyond the detection budget; worst cause SWF-006.C1 (An RX check lags only after 5 nominal periods plus one 10 ms safety-task period (0x1D2 about 0.16 s, 0x226 about 0.14 s, 0x260 0.11 s, 0xAA about 0.07 s); the budget is not yet confirmed against an FTTI (HARA OI-004) or against real inter-frame gaps (tools/can_gaps); O 4, D 3, AP H); detection: Per-message 5-period timeout test for every Toyota RX check, in the CI safety suite BE-1.14 (MCU fault sets controls_allowed (BE-1.07 class)) → DFM-003: Safety state in SRAM corrupted (controls_allowed, limits, counters, stack); worst cause DFM-003.C1 (Double-bit soft error or permanent SRAM fault; RAMECC monitors not configured, ECC interrupt not registered; O 3, D 10, AP H); detection: No LionDriver hardware verification or qualification test exists for this cause (WP-H-06/WP-H-07 not started; no HIL bench, D-04) BE-1.25 (Envelope software defect in the not-allowed torque check or the controls_allowed bookkeeping (lateral.h:111-114), e.g. a cruise edge refused for MAIN_ON = 0 left the engagement window open (SM-F1, SWF-089; reference build fixed at BL-006, opendbc#17)) → SWF-002, SWF-055, SWF-089: Steering torque passed while controls are not allowed; worst cause SWF-002.C1 (Defect in the not-allowed torque check (lateral.h:111-114) or in controls_allowed bookkeeping; O 5, D 3, AP H); detection: opendbc safety suite with 100% line coverage and mutation tests, run by fork CI on every change (.github/workflows/safety.yaml, CR-CI-05). At BL-002 the Toyota tests pass locally (287, 34 skipped); mutation was last run locally at BL-001 (2705/2705 killed). Tests are derived from the implementation, not from requirements

svg.text: SG-03: 29 events (backed 25, by design 1, external 3, unbacked 0); 43 FMEA modes reach SG-03 (in the tree 32, justified 11, tree gaps 0)
Worst cause: highest AP, then highest D. Red: single-point path from the gate logic. Text cut with … is given in full in the figure description.
